title: Automated Compliance for Hybrid Cloud Financial Services
business: A regional financial services provider managing sensitive customer data across distributed hybrid cloud environments.
problem: The organization faces significant operational overhead and security risks due to inconsistent patching cycles and manual configuration drift across their RHEL-based virtual machines and OpenShift clusters.
solution: The organization implements Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform to orchestrate configuration management and security patching, integrated with Red Hat OpenShift to provide a consistent container orchestration layer. By utilizing Red Hat Hardened Images, the team ensures that all deployed workloads start from a secure, prescanned baseline, reducing the attack surface across the hybrid cloud.
steps: Standardize all virtual machine and container base layers using Red Hat Hardened Images to ensure security compliance from the point of deployment.
Deploy Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform to create standardized playbooks for automated patching and configuration enforcement across the RHEL fleet.
Integrate OpenShift Virtualization to manage legacy virtual machines alongside containerized workloads within a single management plane.
Configure automated workflows to trigger security scans and remediation tasks whenever a configuration drift is detected by the automation platform.
outcome: The organization achieves a unified operational posture where security compliance is enforced programmatically, significantly reducing the time spent on manual audit preparation and patching cycles.
limitation: A primary limitation is the increased complexity in managing the automation control plane itself; if the Ansible controller becomes misconfigured, it can propagate errors across the entire infrastructure. This can be checked by monitoring the controller's task logs and audit trails for failed execution patterns.
